question: Should OpenClaw land this Android Installed Apps disclosure gate with legacy opt-ins disabled until renewed consent, plus the new Google Play Data Safety CSV release lane?
rationale: The code path handles privacy-sensitive installed-app inventory and intentionally changes upgrade behavior, while Play acceptance depends on release materials that source review cannot fully validate.

options.title: Accept the privacy rollout
options.body: Merge after the branch is conflict-free if a maintainer confirms the disclosure wording, legacy opt-in reset, Data Safety CSV, and privacy-policy/review materials are aligned.

options.title: Adjust wording or placement first
options.body: Update the disclosure or settings flow if Play review or privacy counsel requires a different prominent-disclosure presentation, then repeat emulator proof.

options.title: Hold until release materials are ready
options.body: Keep the branch open if the code, Play Console declaration, privacy-policy update, and release timing should ship together but are not ready yet.

recommendation.title: Accept the privacy rollout
recommendation.body: Merge after the branch is conflict-free if a maintainer confirms the disclosure wording, legacy opt-in reset, Data Safety CSV, and privacy-policy/review materials are aligned.

likelyOwner.reason: He supplied the branch, Play Console validation context, and release-lane changes, making him the best available owner to confirm the rollout materials before broader maintainer approval.
